<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>The main result of this note is that if <jats:italic>I</jats:italic> is an ideal generated by a regular double summability matrix summability method <jats:italic>T</jats:italic> that is the product of two nonnegative regular matrix methods for single sequences, then <jats:italic>I</jats:italic>-statistical convergence and convergence in <jats:italic>I</jats:italic>-density are equivalent. In particular, the method <jats:italic>T</jats:italic> generates a density <jats:italic>µ<jats:sub>T</jats:sub>
                  </jats:italic> with the additive property (AP) and hence, the additive property for null sets (APO). The densities used to generate statistical convergence, lacunary statistical convergence, and general de la Vallée-Poussin statistical convergence are generated by these types of double summability methods. If a matrix <jats:italic>T</jats:italic> generates a density with the additive property then <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>-statistical convergence, convergence in <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>-density and strong <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>-summabilty are equivalent for bounded sequences. An example is given to show that not every regular double summability matrix generates a density with additve property for null sets.</jats:p>
title: Ideal convergence generated by double summability methods
